Prior to the unification of Norway, Western Scandinavia was divided into a number of petty kingdoms (). Some were as small as a cluster of villages, while others comprised several of today's counties.
The exact number and size of the petty kingdoms is unknown, as there are no contemporary written sources concerning this time period of Norwegian history. The kings' sagas and legendary sagas, which were written in Iceland in the 12th and 13th centuries, are the primary means of knowledge about the events of this time period. As these sagas primarily concerned mythological kings and their primary function was entertainment, their reliability as historical sources is in dispute.
Historicity
Kingdoms and earldoms
Agder
The Kingdom of Agder was located on the southern tip of Norway. The modern-day county of Agder is roughly coextensive with the kingdom's territory.
Fjordane
The Kingdom of Fjordane was located in western Norway near modern-day Bergen.
